title: Aged Balance and the Payment Plan Term — Insulin Pump Program Collections Standard
content:
**Standard.** The aged-balance reduction of a payment plan on an Insulin Pump Program follows how much of the program balance is aged. A posting counts as aged when its posting date is on or before the same day of the month 4 months (the aged months) before the acceptance date, and the aged balance is the aged postings — remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds — less every payment and balance adjustment on the program, never below zero.

| Aged balance compared with the program balance | Program balance | Effect on the plan months |
|---|---|---|
| more than a third | at least $300.00 (the mid-term ceiling) | 2 months (the large aged reduction) taken off |
| more than a third | below $300.00 | 1 month (the small aged reduction) taken off |
| a third or less | any | nothing taken off |

The program balance is the remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds posted on the program less its payments and balance adjustments.

## Worked cases (hypothetical, acceptance on 10 September)

- Postings dated on or before 10 May count as aged; a posting dated 11 May does not.
- Program balance $600.00; aged postings $400.00 less $100.00 of payments: aged balance $300.00, more than a third of $600.00 ($200.00); the balance is at least $300.00, so 2 months are taken off.
- Program balance $240.00; aged balance $80.00: exactly a third is not more than a third, so nothing is taken off.
